claude_take: Every AI story today is really about who gets to say no. Google ships a model explicitly built for cyber defense, but Bank of America is busy telling customers the opposite lesson -- don't hand your passwords to an agent, because liability doesn't move with convenience. Pew's healthcare numbers land in the same place: people will take AI's help, but only if a person still signs off. Meta's publishers are fighting the same fight at industrial scale, just over data instead of passwords. It's a pattern now -- the infrastructure races ahead while every institution downstream quietly builds a wall around the one thing it still wants a human to decide. Even the non-AI stories read that way: Hello Sunshine shrinking back to the handful of things its founder actually wants to make by hand, and Versace restaging its slowest, most human craft in couture rather than rushing out another ready-to-wear drop. The industry keeps selling automation; the market keeps buying reassurance that someone is still in the room.
claude_take_title: Every AI Story Is About Who Says No

items.headline: Google Launches Gemini 4 Carbon, a Model Built for Cyber Defense and Long-Horizon Tasks
items.summary: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon, calling it its strongest model yet, with a particular focus on cybersecurity and long-horizon engineering problems. The company says the model leads rival systems at finding software vulnerabilities and is more than twice as likely as its predecessor, Gemini 4 Argon, to write secure code on internal benchmarks. Carbon is rolling out this week to a limited group of cybersecurity defenders before a wider release, as Google leans into AI's role on both sides of digital security. The launch keeps Google in a tight three-way race with OpenAI and Anthropic over which lab holds the strongest frontier model.

items.headline: Bank of America Tells Customers Not to Share Banking Passwords With AI Agents
items.summary: Bank of America emailed customers warning them against handing their banking usernames and passwords to AI agents and other outside services, saying account holders remain responsible for anything those agents do with that access. A bank spokesperson confirmed the email, titled 'Protecting your finances in the AI World,' is authentic. It follows similar moves by Chase, Citi, and Morgan Stanley as banks scramble to set rules for agentic AI before it causes real financial harm. The email is a sign of how far ahead of the rules the rush to let AI act on people's behalf has gotten.

items.headline: Sir Patrick Stewart, Star of Star Trek and X-Men, Dies at 86
items.summary: Patrick Stewart, the Shakespeare-trained actor who became one of the most recognizable faces in science fiction as Star Trek's Captain Jean-Luc Picard and the X-Men's Professor Charles Xavier, died at his Los Angeles home, his family announced. His longtime representative said he died after a brief illness involving Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, in the care of his wife and family. Tributes followed from Marvel Studios, former castmates, and the Royal Shakespeare Company, where decades of stage work first made his name before Hollywood did. He was knighted in 2010 for his services to drama.

items.headline: Reese Witherspoon's Hello Sunshine Cuts Roughly Half Its Staff After Buyback
items.summary: Weeks after Reese Witherspoon and Mediawan bought Hello Sunshine back from Candle Media at a steep discount to the $900 million Candle paid in 2021, the production company laid off roughly 30 employees, about half its remaining staff. The cuts fall mainly on the direct-to-consumer side of the business, which had tried to turn Witherspoon's fans into customers for branded content and products. The remaining team will focus on the film, television, and book-club work Witherspoon has said she actually wants to make. It's one of the more visible retreats yet from the celebrity-studio boom of the early 2020s.

items.headline: Meta Indefinitely Delays Its New AI and Commercial Terms After Publisher Pushback
items.summary: Meta announced it is indefinitely postponing revised commercial terms that would have broadened its rights to use publisher and advertiser content to train its AI systems. The move follows weeks of complaints to EU and UK antitrust regulators from publishers and advertisers who argued the terms gave Meta an effectively unlimited license over their content. Meta says it is consulting further and will explain more about how its web crawlers work, while maintaining the backlash misreads the terms. The European Publishers Council says the delay isn't enough and wants the terms suspended entirely while regulators investigate.

items.headline: Pew: Americans Are Open to AI in Healthcare but Want a Human Making the Final Call
items.summary: A new Pew Research Center survey of nearly 3,500 US adults finds broad comfort with AI handling administrative healthcare tasks like translation and scheduling, but sharp discomfort with AI making diagnosis or treatment decisions on its own -- only about 5% would allow that without any human review. Roughly half of adults say AI will ultimately make the doctor-patient relationship worse, and a similar share worry it will weaken the privacy of their health information. The findings suggest a narrow, conditional path for AI in medicine: useful as an assistant, not trusted as a decision-maker.

items.headline: Versace to Return to Paris Haute Couture in January, Marking Pieter Mulier's Debut
items.summary: Versace confirmed that Atelier Versace will return to the Paris Haute Couture calendar in January 2027 for the first time since 2016, with new chief creative officer Pieter Mulier presenting his debut collection for the house. Mulier, who joined Versace from Alaïa earlier this year under Prada Group's ownership, will show couture before ready-to-wear, reversing the order most new designers follow. The choice signals how seriously Prada Group is investing in rebuilding Versace's top-tier craft credentials rather than rushing out a commercial collection, and it's a bet that couture's visibility can reset the narrative around a house that has struggled since its sale by Capri Holdings.

items.headline: Nearly One in Five Women Treated for Anxiety or Depression Also Have ADHD, Study Finds
items.summary: A new study found that close to 20% of women seeking treatment for anxiety or depression also met criteria for ADHD, and nearly half of those cases had never been previously diagnosed. The researchers suggest ADHD's inattentive symptoms are often mistaken for, or masked by, mood disorders in women, delaying proper diagnosis and treatment for years. The findings add to a growing body of research on how ADHD presents differently and gets missed more often in women than in men. Clinicians treating women for anxiety or depression who aren't improving as expected may need to screen for ADHD specifically.

items.headline: Kant's Categorical Imperative
items.summary: Immanuel Kant argued that moral actions must be guided by principles you could will to become universal law for everyone, not rules that merely happen to suit your own desires or circumstances. His categorical imperative says to act only according to a maxim you could consistently want everyone else to follow, which is why Kant treats lying or using people merely as means to your own ends as always wrong, regardless of the outcome. Unlike systems that judge actions by their consequences, Kant's ethics judges them by the reasoning behind them, and by whether that reasoning respects other people as ends in themselves. The idea still shapes modern debates about rights, duties, and what we owe each other independent of results.
items.summary_fr: Emmanuel Kant soutient que nos actions morales doivent reposer sur des principes que l'on pourrait vouloir voir devenir une loi universelle, valable pour tous, et non de simples règles commodes pour nos désirs du moment. Son impératif catégorique invite à n'agir que selon une maxime que l'on pourrait vouloir voir suivie par tout le monde sans contradiction, ce qui explique pourquoi Kant juge le mensonge ou l'instrumentalisation d'autrui toujours moralement condamnables, quelles que soient les conséquences. Contrairement aux morales qui jugent les actes à leurs résultats, l'éthique kantienne les juge à l'intention qui les sous-tend et au respect qu'elle porte à chaque personne comme fin en soi. Cette idée continue d'irriguer les débats contemporains sur les droits, les devoirs et ce que nous nous devons les uns aux autres, indépendamment des conséquences.
